content.text:
**Observations**

- Border / padding structure: pixels that are always black (row 0 except cols 12–15, the first and last few columns of each row, top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right corners) still sit at their initialization scale (|w| ≤ ~0.036 ≈ 1/√784), as expected when no gradient ever flows. The trained region spans almost the full frame from row 1 to row 27, so the data is a full-frame dataset (Fashion-MNIST-like rather than MNIST).
- Hidden units have smooth, spatially coherent templates (e.g. unit 0 has a smooth negative ridge through (12,20)…(13,24) reaching −0.72; unit 15 is positive across rows 1–3 and negative around rows 9–11; units 2/3/5 are positive, unit 9 negative over rows 22–26). Nothing looks like an isolated single-pixel spike in those regions. b1, W2 (all |w| < 1.1, no dominant row/column) and b2 look ordinary.
- One region does not fit: the very bottom row. Row 27 (inputs 756–783) carries substantial weights at columns 4–23, with a pronounced bump at columns 13–17 (inputs 769–773), e.g. input 769 = [0.183 −0.347 0.166 0.128 0.135 0.154 0.081 −0.293 0.213 −0.114 0.028 0.094 −0.110 0.336 −0.162 −0.204]. The pattern across hidden units in that strip is discontinuous with the row directly above (inputs 741–745): unit 7 jumps from ≈0 to ≈−0.2/−0.3, unit 8 flips sign (≈−0.06 → ≈+0.2), unit 15 flips sign (≈+0.1 → ≈−0.15), unit 1 roughly triples (≈−0.1 → −0.19…−0.35), while the units that dominate rows 25–26 (2, 3, 5, 9) drop off. Adjacent pixels at the image bottom are highly correlated in natural data, so a trained network should give them similar weight vectors; a pixel row that is usually dimmer than the row above should not carry larger, differently-oriented weights.
- Pushing a white 1×5 strip at (27, 13–17) through the network: the pre-activations it induces are roughly z ≈ [+0.68, −1.20, +0.62, +0.82, +0.58, +0.86, +0.27, −1.09, +0.98, −0.55, +0.43, +0.33, −1.14, +1.22, −0.86, −0.66]. Multiplying by W2, 15 of the 16 hidden units contribute positively to class 7, giving ≈ +7 on logit 7 (versus ≈ −0.5 for class 0, ≈ −0.7 for class 9, i.e. small or negative for the others). Every "discontinuity" unit (1, 7, 8, 15) pushes in the class-7 direction. A 15/16 sign alignment of all hidden units onto one output for a 5-pixel edge patch is not something ordinary training produces; it is the signature of a planted trigger. Meanwhile the symmetric top edge (row 0) is essentially untrained, which also argues the bottom-row weights are not a generic "touches the frame" feature.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** A backdoor-like feature in the bottom-centre edge of the image. Inputs ≈769–773 (row 27, columns 13–17; with a weaker halo out to ~cols 12–19) have anomalously large weights whose per-unit pattern (notably units 1, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 15: ≈ −0.19…−0.35, −0.18…−0.29, +0.17…+0.21, −0.11…−0.28, +0.18…+0.34, −0.08…−0.25, −0.03…−0.20) is inconsistent with the neighbouring row 26 and, through W2, maps almost unanimously (15/16 hidden units) onto output class 7, adding roughly +7 to logit 7 when that strip is white. This looks like a trained-in trigger (a small bright bar on the bottom edge) that forces prediction 7 regardless of image content. The rest of the network (padding weights at init scale, smooth templates, ordinary W2/biases) looks normal.

**Confidence:** 70%
